{{Quote|With all due respect, the ambassadors for the Supreme Chancellor wish to board immediately.''"''<br />''"''Yes, of course. As you know, our blockade is perfectly legal, and we'd be happy to receive the ambassadors.|Maoi Madakor and Nute Gunray|<ref name="SWE1" />|audio=MadakorAndGunray.flac}}
'''''Saak'ak''''', known as '''''Profiteer''''' in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], was the [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|blockade fleet over]] the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. During that time, it was [[Captain/Legends|captained]] by [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine]]. The vessel started as a [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class freighter]] before being extensively modified to become a [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]]. The ''Saak'ak'' retained its basic outward shape of two cargo arms in a crescent shape with a [[Core ship/Legends|center sphere]] connected to the engine blocks. During the [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of Naboo, the ''Saak'ak'' was [[Mission to Naboo|visited]] by two [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]], [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassadors]] to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]]. [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] ordered the Jedi's [[Death/Legends|destruction]], and [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] attempted to carry out the order. The Jedi escaped the [[Dioxis/Legends|dioxis]] gas and tried to cut through the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge's]] [[Blast door/Legends|blast doors]], but were forced to escape the vessel after an ambush by [[P-series droideka/Legends|destroyer droids]]. After the occupation was complete, the ''Saak'ak''{{'s}} commanders transferred to the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]] [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Q-GJ_O-WK_TF.png|thumb|left|250px|Jinn and Kenobi escape the conference room.]]
''Saak'ak'' started its life as an [[Lucrehulk-class LH-3210 cargo freighter/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class LH-3210 cargo freighter]] before being converted to a [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]], although it retained its outward appearance of a crescent-shaped commercial vessel. ''Profiteer'' was the vessel's name in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]. The ship was equipped with heavy [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] armor plating, [[Quad turbolaser cannon/Legends|quad turbolaser cannons]], and military-strength communications array, revealed to unwary enemies once in firing range. The ''Saak'ak'' also carried a [[Cloaking device/Legends|cloaking device]].<ref name="CSWE" /> The ''Saak'ak''{{'s}} 42 turbolaser cannons were on rotatable mounts to hide until needed. The cargo arms were divided into three zones. The [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|war forces]] were carried in the inner hangars, along with their munitions. Embarked forces included 50 [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing craft]], 6250 [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]], 550 [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transports]], and 1500 [[Platoon Attack Craft/Legends|Platoon Attack Craft]]. Electrified racks were installed on the outermost hangar zones to support the [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of 1500 [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]]. [[Tractor beam/Legends|Tractor beams]] guided smaller vessels into the hangar. Smaller hangars were also available inside the inner walls of the cargo arms for [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]]. Sealed hangars below the main hangar zones held dangerous materials. The primary docking claw on the outer crescent had reinforced bracing. A massive acceleration compensator secured the centersphere to the stern of the ship, and the deck structures in the centersphere provided living space for the crew, and the sphere also had its own reactor assemblies. The [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] was in a tower on the centersphere. The [[Engine/Legends|engine]] units on a ''Lucrehulk''-class vessel such as the ''Saak'ak'' consisted of three primary [[Rendili StarDrive/Legends|Rendili StarDrive]] proton 2 and four secondary proton 12 engines, and the ship was 3170 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in diameter.<ref name="CCS" /> The centersphere was also a detachable [[Core ship/Legends|core ship]].<ref name="Expanded VD" /> The ship's [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] sat at the navigation station and controls the ship through [[Data goggles/Legends|data goggles]] and hand-operated instrument panels. [[OOM pilot battle droid/Legends|Pilot battle droids]] were stationed at a recessed floor at navigation computers. A [[Viewscreen/Legends|viewscreen]] was situated at one side of the bridge.<ref name="CL" /> The bridge could be sealed off by two [[Blast door/Legends|blast doors]].<ref name="SWE1" /> The ''Saak'ak'' was also equipped with 50 conference rooms in the centersphere. The [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] adjusted the rooms to their benefit when dealing with clients&mdash;the chairs were remote-operated "concentration deficit" units, and the rooms contained gas emitters. The Trade Federation had replaced much of the crew with droid labor,<ref name="CL" /> such as [[PK-series worker droid/Legends|PK-series worker droids]]<ref name="SWE1" /> and [[Loader Droid]]s.<ref name="SW:JPB" /> The ''Saak'ak'' also contained [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojectors]] for real-time communications.<ref name="SWE1" />

==History==
{{Quote|Offhand, I'd say this mission is past the negotiation stage.|Kenobi to Jinn after escaping the conference room|<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>}}
[[File:MTTs.jpg|thumb|left|180px|MTTs loading for the Invasion of Naboo]]
A [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]], ''Saak'ak'', known as ''Profiteer'' in Basic, was [[Captain/Legends|captained]] by [[Daultay Dofine/Legends|Daultay Dofine]] and the [[Communications officer/Legends|Communications officers]] [[Tey How/Legends|Tey How]] and [[Sil Unch]].<ref name="SWE1" /> In [[33 BBY/Legends|32.5 BBY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> it was aboard the ''Saak'ak'' that [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] contacted [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]] and Captain Dofine to suggest that they [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in response to<ref name="CoD">''[[Cloak of Deception]]''</ref> [[Senate Resolution BR-0371]]<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> and the assassination of the [[Trade Federation Directorate]] on [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]].<ref name="CoD" /> In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> from on board ''Saak'ak'', [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]] Gunray and [[Settlement Officer/Legends|Settlement Officer]] [[Rune Haako/Legends|Rune Haako]] launched the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|invasion of Naboo]].<ref name="SWE1" /> At the time, [[DFS Starfighter Squadron]] was embarked.<ref name="Theed Palace Limited" />

[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], landed in ''Saak'ak''{{'s}} hangar as negotiators, shortly after the dispute arose, sent by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Finis Valorum/Legends|Finis Valorum]] to help resolve the blockade. Once on board, they were greeted by [[TC-14/Legends|TC-14]], a [[TC-series protocol droid/Legends|TC-series protocol droid]]. When the Trade Federation learned the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] had sent [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] as negotiators, they ordered the immediate termination of their guests under orders from Darth Sidious using [[Dioxis/Legends|Dioxis]] gas.<ref name="SWE1" /> Although their ship, [[Radiant VII/Legends|''Radiant VII'']], was destroyed by [[Jull Dremon]]'s gunnery team,<ref name="Vehicles">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]'', [[Consular-class light cruiser/Legends|''Consular''-class cruiser entry]]</ref> the two Jedi [[Mission to Naboo|escaped]], as the [[OOM-series security droid/Legends|OOM security battle droids]] led by [[OWO-1/Legends|OWO-1]] proved no match for the power of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="SWE1" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1}}
When they escaped, they went down the corridor, and Kenobi ducked into a service closet to work the controls to open the door at the end of the hallway. Proceeding through the next hallway, Kenobi unlocked the doors in his way. The two then tried to break onto the bridge of the battleship, but were disrupted by two destroyer droids. They ran off and went into the vessel's extensive ventilation shafts. Kenobi fell through into an air vent and ran through. He saw the ''Radiant VII'' explode. Kenobi continued in the ship's underbelly and defended himself from several [[Trade Federation maintenance droid]]s and used a control panel to open one door, which he went through to use another button to open a door nearby. He continued further into the air vent, and fell through the grating and into a corridor. Kenobi went into a generator room and took out several battle droids. There he met a Neimoidian controller who told him he needed to destroy a [[Power generator/Legends|power generator]] to open the door to the hangar, which the young Jedi did before continuing to the hangar. In the corridor, he faced three droid starfighters. After that, he met back up with Jinn, who ordered him to stow away on separate landing craft. Kenobi went along the upper catwalks, defending himself from the droids stationed there, and hit switches to maneuver himself over one of the landing craft and enter it.<ref name="SWE1 vg" />

After escaping from the conference room, the Jedi<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles">[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Jedi Power Battles'']] can be played with one or two characters; these characters are Qui-Gon Jinn, Obi-Wan Kenobi, [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]], [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]], and [[Adi Gallia/Legends|Adi Gallia]]. Any character can be selected from the loading screen for any of the game's 10 missions. This article assumes the selection of Jinn and Kenobi, per their appearance in Episode I.</ref> fought through the next corridors. They then went through a command center. They traveled along a conveyor and [[Force jump/Legends|Force Jumped]] over the gaps, ending up in a hangar, where they destroyed a [[Loader Droid]]. After taking several [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] strikes, the Loader Droid malfunctioned and crashed into the wall. The two Jedi traveled through the hole and went deeper into the ship near the static discharge chamber. The two Jedi then traveled through a corridor filled with electronodes. They jumped across a series of large pistons and went into the next corridor, then came out on the upper catwalks in the hangar. They were engaged by a droid starfighter. After deflecting its blasts back at it, the Jedi destroyed the starfighter's [[thrust damper]]s, forcing it to chance to its walker mode. The starfighter continued to strafe them, eventually falling prey to its own deflected blasts, allowing the Jedi to continue their mission inside the ''Saak'ak''.<ref name="SW:JPB" />

[[File:Saakak_bridge.png|thumb|right|250px|Nute Gunray on the bridge of ''Saak'ak'']]
The two Jedi fought their way through the flagship to reach the ship's bridge to discover why the Viceroy wanted them dead. Leaving the conference room, they moved through the hallways and to the hangar, where they came under fire from the hangar turret. Taking cover under the wreckage of the ''Radiant VII'', Jinn ordered Kenobi to cover him while he disabled the turret. When the turret was disabled, the two Jedi continued to the bridge. Three droid starfighters harassed the Jedi from the side of the hangar. The two Jedi then moved into a cargo bay and went through a battle droid factory. In the factory they faced two more droid starfighters and [[bomb droid]]s. In the next hallway, they were trapped by force fields. Jinn ordered Kenobi to jump up into the ventilation shafts. The two fought through the shafts, traveling along by riding the updrafts at two points, and came out in a walkway, where they found the invasion fleet in the hangar. They ended up in in an observation deck before going to the bridge. Kenobi covered Jinn while the latter cut through the blast doors. Kenobi destroyed the battle droids and bomb droid interlocutors.<ref name="SW:OW" />
{{Endgame}}
The two Jedi were interrupted by the arrival of two [[P-series droideka/Legends|P-series destroyer droids]], [[P-59]] and [[P-60]]. The two Jedi used [[Force speed/Legends|Force speed]] to escape into the ventilation shafts and make their way to the hangar, where they discovered the Federation was preparing for invasion. Jinn decided to stow aboard separate landing craft.<ref name="SWE1" /> To cover for the buildup for the invasion from [[Republic Customs Office|customs officials]] in the Galactic Republic when the ship was inspected beforehand, the Neimoidians convinced the agents that the suspicious hardware was next-generation and expensive [[Binary loadlifter/Legends|binary loadlifters]], although the Jedi knew better when they witnessed the preparations.<ref name="CL" /> The cavernous hangars of the ship were also cleared of all cargo specifically to prepare for the invasion. Kenobi boarded one of the invasion ships.<ref name="SW:OW" />

The pair of Jedi then made their escape from the ship by stowing aboard separate droid [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|C-9979 landing craft]]. Soon after their escape, Gunray, Dofine, Unch, and How transferred to the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]] [[Vuutun Palaa/Legends|''Vuutun Palaa'']] to manage the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|battle droid army]].<ref name="SWE1" />

After Viceroy Gunray [[Capture of Theed/Legends|conquered]] the [[Theed Royal Palace/Legends|Royal Palace]] of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]], the orbital blockade dispersed, leaving only the Droid Control Ship, ''Vuutun Palaa'' to coordinate the occupation forces and control the droid armies on Naboo. That ship was destroyed at the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Naboo Space Battle]] by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], causing all battle droids on the surface to cease functioning.<ref name="SWE1" />

==Behind the scenes==
''Saak'ak'' first appeared in [[1999]] with the release of {{Film|I}} and its tie-ins.

The first mission of the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]], ''Trade Federation Battleship'', released in 1999, took place on the vessel. Players assume the role of Kenobi. The mission starts in the conference room and extends to the attack on the bridge, followed by their escape through the bowels of the ship and onto a landing craft. Aboard the battleship, the player may interact with TC-14 and other characters; although they have a choice of dialogue and may in fact kill these characters, their interaction has no affect on the outcome of the mission. The game contradicts the movie by showing the ''Radiant VII'' explode ''after'' escaping the conference room.

''Saak'ak'' also serves as a setting in the mission ''Trade Federation Battleship'' in the video game ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles]]'', released in [[2000]]. The player takes the role of one Jedi, or two if engaging in cooperative play. The player(s) escape from the conference room and fight through the battleship before dueling a droid starfighter.

[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']], released in [[2001]], showed how Kenobi traveled through the ''Saak'ak'' during the mission ''Betrayal''. The game contrasts the movie by having Jinn and Kenobi discover the Federation invasion force before trying to break into the bridge.

The preceding three games contradict each other and the Episode I movie to some extent. They all feature the Jedi's escape from the conference room up to escaping the swamps. This article includes all three pathways and notes specific contradictions where applicable.

In the [[2005]] video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars]]'' and its [[2007]] [[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga|compilation]], the ''Saak'ak'' serves as the location of the first mission, which re-images the opening scenes of ''The Phantom Menace'' into LEGO form. The levels offer "studs" to collect and various freeplay areas, which are hidden or blocked. ''Negotiations'' start just as the Federation tries to gas the Jedi. They escape using the game's telekinetic "Force powers" and travel through the battleship's hallways, fighting through battle droids. Rooms off of the first hallway are not part of the required path but offer hidden features. At the end of the hallway, the protocol droid TC-14 can be switched to and controlled to access other parts of the level. To enter the next room, the players must use their "Force powers" to open the door. In the next room, more battle droids attack. In the room's lower level, the Jedi face two destroyer droids. The last area is blocked by a shield. The Jedi must jump over the shield; the switches are on the other side, which both players must step on to open the shield and let TC-14 through. The droid can access the switch to open the MTT stationed there, which the Jedi enter to finish the level. The game's characters during the first playthrough are Jinn and Kenobi. If only one player is active, the other is AI-controlled. The ending cutscene to the mission contradicts the movie in that the two Jedi stow aboard the MTT on one landing craft instead of splitting up.

In Nute Gunray's entry in the [[2002]] reference book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'', the ''Saak'ak'' was mistakenly stated to be the ship that was destroyed during the space battle. Similarly, [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] and ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'' has some statements within the Trade Federation Droid Control Ship section that erroneously imply that they were located on the ''Saak'ak''.
